title: Baby essentials checklist
intro: A list for the first 3 months. Labels: essential, useful, depends. Quantities assume washing every 2–3 days.

sections.title: Clothes (size 56–62)
sections.tip: Size 56 can be too small after 2–4 weeks. Buy more in 62 and only a few pieces in 56. Wash everything in a mild, fragrance-free detergent before first use.

items.name: Sleepsuits (ideally with front snaps or a zip)
Warm hat, snowsuit or stroller footmuff
items.why: Depends on the season. The Weather module covers autumn, spring and winter.

sections.title: Sleep
sections.tip: Details and buying criteria for the cot, bedside crib and mattress are in the Room & sleep module.

items.name: Cot or bedside crib attached to the parents' bed
New mattress that fits the cot exactly
Baby sleeping bag (instead of a duvet)
items.why: Match the thickness (TOG) to the room temperature. A sleeping bag can't slide over the face like a duvet.

items.name: Muslin or cotton cloths
items.why: Changing mat, bib, sun shade, towel. The most versatile item on the list.

items.name: Disposable nappies, size 1
items.why: Don't stockpile. Newborns move to size 2 quickly and a brand may not suit you.

items.name: Cotton pads, gauze and warm water, or water-based wipes
Baby bath with stand or insert
Bath thermometer
items.why: Bath water about 37°C. Your elbow works too.

items.name: Changing mat with raised sides or a changing top for a dresser
Breast pump
items.why: Buy or rent only when you need it. A lactation consultant can help pick the type.

items.name: Bottles 150–250 ml
items.why: For formula feeding. If breastfeeding, 1–2 as backup are enough.

items.name: Infant formula
items.why: Choose after talking to a midwife or paediatrician.

items.name: Infant car seat 0–13 kg or 40–87 cm
items.why: Needed on the way home from hospital. Don't buy a used one with unknown history: after a crash it loses its protective properties.

items.name: Stroller with a (deep) carrycot
items.why: Babies up to about 6 months should lie flat.

items.name: Ergonomic carrier or wrap
items.why: Legs in an M position, face visible, close enough to kiss the top of the head.

items.name: Documents: ID, pregnancy record, test results, blood type
Cot bumpers
items.why: They increase the risk of suffocation and SIDS. Paediatricians clearly advise against them.

items.name: Pillow and duvet for a baby
items.why: Until 12 months the cot should be empty. Use a sleeping bag instead of a duvet.

items.name: Sleep wedges and positioners
items.why: They don't reduce SIDS risk and a baby can press their face into them.

items.name: Baby walker
items.why: Frequent injuries (falls down stairs) and no benefit for learning to walk. A sturdy push walker is better.

items.name: Shoes for a baby who can't walk yet
items.why: Socks or warm stroller booties are enough.

items.name: Wipe warmers and other single-purpose gadgets
Used car seat with unknown history
